skill.name: m365-agents-ts
skill.description: Build Microsoft 365 agents with TypeScript, Express hosting, AgentApplication routing, streaming responses, and Copilot Studio client integrations.

security_audit.summary: Static analysis mainly flagged Markdown code fences, documentation links, and environment variable examples in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious automation intent was found. The skill is documentation-oriented, but authors should keep stronger warnings around secrets and production validation.

remediation.issue: Secret placeholders appear in environment variable examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning near the environment block that users must never paste real API keys or bearer tokens into prompts or source files.

remediation.issue: Samples rely on required environment variables without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Show startup validation for required Microsoft 365, Azure OpenAI, and Copilot Studio settings before connecting clients.

remediation.issue: The examples are snippets, not production-ready applications.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for authentication, authorization, logging redaction, and error handling before deploying agents to Teams or Microsoft 365.

content.value_statement: Developers need reliable patterns for Microsoft 365 agents across Teams and Copilot Studio. This skill provides TypeScript examples for routing, hosting, streaming, and Copilot Studio integration.
actual_capabilities: Lists Microsoft 365 Agents SDK packages for TypeScript projects.
Shows an Express-hosted AgentApplication routing pattern.
Demonstrates streaming responses with Azure OpenAI and Teams labels.
Provides an invoke activity handling example.
Shows Copilot Studio client and WebChat integration patterns.
Links to Microsoft Learn and GitHub sample references.
limitations: It does not verify current SDK signatures by itself.
It does not include a complete authentication or token acquisition flow.
The examples are snippets, not a full production application.
Users must provide their own Azure and Copilot Studio configuration.

use_cases.title: Create a Teams agent starter
use_cases.description: Use the hosting and routing examples to plan a basic TypeScript agent for Teams or Microsoft 365.

use_cases.title: Plan Copilot Studio integration
use_cases.description: Compare direct client and WebChat patterns before connecting an existing Copilot Studio agent.

use_cases.title: Add streaming answers
use_cases.description: Use the streaming response pattern to design long-running Azure OpenAI responses with status updates.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript starter plan for a Microsoft 365 agent using AgentApplication and Express hosting. Include required packages and main files.

prompt_templates.title: Add Message Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design message and conversation update handlers for a Teams agent. Keep each handler focused and explain required TurnContext use.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate Streaming Responses
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a streaming response flow for Azure OpenAI in a Microsoft 365 agent. Include labels, progress updates, and final stream cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Microsoft 365 Agents SDK design for production readiness. Check authentication, environment variables, logging, error handling, and Copilot Studio integration.

output_examples.input: Plan a starter Microsoft 365 agent for Teams using TypeScript.
output_examples.output: A concise build plan with packages, hosting choices, routing handlers, configuration needs, and documentation checks before coding.

output_examples.input: Review a streaming response handler for a Teams agent.
output_examples.output: A focused review covering progress updates, sensitivity labels, stream completion, error handling, and safe Azure OpenAI configuration.

output_examples.input: Choose a Copilot Studio integration approach.
output_examples.output: A comparison of direct client and WebChat options, including setup needs, token handling, user experience, and deployment considerations.

best_practices: Verify current Microsoft SDK signatures before generating final code.
Keep secrets in managed stores or environment variables, and validate them at startup.
Add authentication, payload validation, and redacted logging before production deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys, client secrets, or bearer tokens into prompts or source files.
Do not treat the snippets as a complete production security model.
Do not log invoke payloads or Copilot replies without review and redaction.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps plan and draft TypeScript agents for Microsoft 365, Teams, and Copilot Studio.

faq.question: Does it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It lists package commands as documentation, and the user decides whether to run them.

faq.question: Can it verify the latest SDK version?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to check Microsoft documentation and npm before final implementation.

faq.question: Does it include authentication code?
faq.answer: No. It shows configuration placeholders and token provider shape, but users must implement secure authentication.

faq.question: Is it specific to Teams?
faq.answer: No. It covers Microsoft 365 agent patterns, including Teams hosting and Copilot Studio integration.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
